provenance.question: does a theta fitted on one registered FAUST pair recover the true vertex correspondence on HELD-OUT pairs, better than uniform weights?
provenance.plan: pi_hat = I/n on a shared index subsample of both meshes (the registered bijection)
provenance.split: SUBJECT-DISJOINT: training and evaluation subjects do not intersect (checked by `check_split`, which exits on violation). Training pair ids come from the training subjects only and every evaluation pair from the test subjects only. An earlier revision of this module had NO such check and its training pairs shared subjects with the evaluation pairs -- that earlier result is pose transfer within seen subjects, not subject transfer
provenance.box_selection: the box width (rel) AND simplex-only are compared by mean miss@5% on VALIDATION pairs drawn from the TRAINING subjects (disjoint from the test subjects and from the training pair). The selected arm is copied to `learned_selected`; every other width is reported on the test pairs too, but took no part in the selection
provenance.box_meaning: rel is the INVERSE box width: theta in [rel/K, 1/(rel*K)], so rel=0.05 is the widest box and rel=0.9 the narrowest; rel=None (learned_simplex) is the whole simplex
provenance.vertex_subsamples: several index subsamples (default seeds 0,1,2); theta is REFITTED per seed because it depends on the sampled vertices
provenance.metric: GEODESIC distance on the target (potpourri3d heat method) between predicted and true vertex, normalised by sqrt(surface area) of the target -- the FAUST protocol. Miss rates at 1% and 5%
provenance.descriptors: K=13: extrinsic xyz (centred, scaled by diameter), log 1-ring area, log curvature, 8 HKS columns; standardised with the pooled source+target mean/std
provenance.groups: sparse (xyz), area, curv, hks -- used by the grouped_uniform capacity control
provenance.block_controls: uniform_hks (8 HKS columns, equal weight) and uniform_late_hks (t = 32/64/128 only, equal weight). The fitted theta loads almost entirely on the late-HKS columns, so these decide whether learning did more than select the block
provenance.engine: relaxed regret loop, box x simplex, prune disabled, HiGHS master
provenance.stats: paired bootstrap over held-out PAIRS (1000 resamples), never over vertices; each pair is first averaged across vertex-subsample seeds (seeds are repeated measures, not independent pairs)
provenance.corner: the fitted theta sits on the box floor/ceiling and the loop reports converged=False; the weights are therefore 'a feasible point the solver accepted', not a proved optimum
provenance.not_sota: this is not a state-of-the-art claim; deep functional maps reach far lower FAUST errors. The claim under test is only that a learned mixture beats hand-weighted ones
